code rather than returning, so it never becomes an `ApplyError`.

ErrorCode.description:
The non-zero exit status the guest commits when validation fails.

Wire-encoded like a Unix exit status: `0` is success, so an `ErrorCode` is always
non-zero. only provides the untyped integer code; [`ReportableError`](crate::ReportableError)
maps codes to typed values with contextual information.

methods.name: The name of a code the validator defines, or `None` for any other non-zero byte.
methods.new: Create an `ErrorCode` from a raw byte, returning `None` for `0`.

PublicValues.description:
Wire layout of the public values committed by the prover.

Layout (185 bytes, little-endian):
```text
 0..152  state                 [u8; 152]  complete State bytes
152..184 verifier_key          [u8; 32]   ([u32; 8] LE words)
184      return_code            u8         (0 = success, >0 = failure)
```

Serialized manually to avoid struct padding; use [`PublicValues::to_bytes`]
and [`PublicValues::parse`] rather than transmuting.

methods.is_success: Return `true` if the public values report success.

methods.serialize: [`PublicValues::to_bytes`] from borrowed parts, without building a `PublicValues`.
methods.validation_error_code: Return the validation error code if this is a failure, or `None` on success.

ReturnCode.description:
A validation result: `None` means success, `Some(ErrorCode)` means failure.

Wire representation is a single `u8`: `0` for success, non-zero for failure.
Every `u8` is a valid `ReturnCode`, so conversion from `u8` is infallible.

RunId.description:
A strongly-typed 8-byte ASCII alphanumeric identifier for proving runs.

Only ASCII digits (`0..=9`), uppercase letters (`A..=Z`), and lowercase letters (`a..=z`)
are permitted (62^8 ≈ 2.18 × 10^14 possible identifiers).

No symbols, path separators, or Unicode characters are allowed. This guarantees that a
`RunId` is always safe to use as a single path component without escaping or path traversal.
